story:
Earl Vone cannot read, and that is why he holds the chisel. In the Uncounted Age he was a scratcher, one of the small demons who cut marks into the walls of the hollow for no reason anyone could discover, and Adremal, who could read the scratches the first lords had left, found that Vone's were the only marks in the long gallery that meant nothing at all. When the First Roll was to be cut, the Chancellor went looking for a hand that would cut exactly what it was told. A clerk who can read may improve a line. A clerk who cannot will cut the shape he is shown. Adremal draws each line in chalk, and Vone cuts the chalk.

He has cut ten Rolls since, every line of them, and he has gouged every line that was struck. His claws are worn to the quick, and since the Third Roll he has used a chisel the Chancellor had struck from Duke Aypol's white metal, which Aypol has asked for back every Roll. The line of Mystemas in the Ninth Roll was his hardest work: the Chancellor's chalk moved the name from high on the wall to the very bottom and drew it a tenth of its old size, and Vone cut it small without knowing whose it was. The imps say Mystemas has never forgiven the hand, though he knows the hand could not read what it cut.

The court tests him. Princes Abdin and Asmoien, who share one line, have each sent him chalk of their own in the night, a line drawn a finger higher than the other's. Vone cut neither, because neither was in the Chancellor's hand, which is the one shape he knows. Since the doors opened he has cut a second kind of line on the Roll of the Visitors, a realm and a number, already struck, and the Chancellor says Vone cuts those faster than any others, since there are no names in them to go wrong.

He stands a little up the slope from the Chancellor's table among the knights and Mutilators of Legion's Own, with the chisel in one hand and a bag of chalk at his belt. He holds an earl's line because the hand that cuts the Rolls must stand above most of what it cuts, and for no other reason, and he seems content with it.
legend: Vone stands on the approach a little above Grand Chancellor Adremal, among the knights and Mutilators of Legion's Own: Tamuel, Olov, Oprionach and Samiol are all within about twelve hundred units. Level 71 and, unlike the rest of the court, a plain NPC rather than an epic one, so he goes down faster than his level suggests. Pull him first and on his own, before the Chancellor; if the approach knights come with him you have the whole slope on you. Players call him the clerk or the chisel and swear the scratches on the approach walls are the demons' kill list, with every raid's number on it. Hibernians say if you read your own name off the wall you will not come back up; Albion clerics say it is only lines of precedence, which is somehow worse.

loremasterTopic.text: Earl Vone, clerk of Grand Chancellor [Adremal], who cannot read and so cuts exactly the lines he is shown in chalk. He has cut all ten Rolls of the court and every line struck from them, and in the Ninth Roll he cut [Mystemas] small.

bookPage: From the notes of a Camelot stonemason who went down behind a column of knights to copy the approach walls: The cutting is the best I have seen, better than any in the city, and the chalk is still on the newest line. Every stroke is even. Every gouge is clean to the same depth. I watched the one who cuts. He held the chisel as I hold mine and set it to a chalk mark and struck, and when I spoke to him he looked at me with no understanding at all. He cannot read what he cuts. A mason who cannot read cannot carve a mistake. I envied him for that, and I am ashamed of it.
